textoCompleto:
Silverman-Anderson Score

PEDIATRICS AND NEONATOLOGY

Clinically assess the degree of respiratory distress in the newborn, essential for management in the NICU.
Newborn Data

Fill out for the Medical Record/PDF Report

Respiratory Parameters
Synchrony between chest and abdomen.

Retraction of the muscles between the ribs.

Sinking of the xiphoid process area.

Opening of the nostrils during inspiration.

Sound emitted during expiration.

Silverman-Anderson Score

Assessment Memory

Suggested NANDA Diagnoses
Based on the assessment of neonatal respiratory distress.

Processing clinical reasoning...

Frequently Asked Questions
Follow more nursing information on our Nursing Forum.

Related Scales
Apgar Scale Assessment of newborn vitality.

Capurro Method Calculation of somatic Gestational Age.

CRIES Scale Pain assessment in the newborn.

Scientific Reference
SILVERMAN, W. A.; ANDERSEN, D. H. A controlled clinical trial of effects of water mist on obstructive respiratory signs, death rate and necropsy findings among premature infants. Pediatrics , v. 17, n. 1, p. 1-10, 1956.

Score Interpretation

No Distress (0)
Newborn in good respiratory condition. Routine care.

Mild Distress (1-3 points)
Initial signs of respiratory difficulty. Requires continuous observation and possible mild O₂ support.

Moderate Distress (4-7 points)
Compromised respiratory status. Intervention needed (CPAP or oxygen therapy) for clinical stabilization.

Severe Distress (≥ 8 points)
Imminent respiratory failure. Consider advanced ventilatory support (Mechanical Ventilation) and admission to NICU.
